newsitem.title: USA: Shopko debt trades off 75 bp, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: Shopko debt trades off 75 bp, trade thin.

text.p: At least one issue of ShopKo Stores Inc's outstanding debt widened by 75 basis points in secondary trade on Tuesday following the announced merger of the company and Phar-Mor Inc, traders said.
ShopKo's nine percent senior notes due 2004 were said to trade at a spread of 220 basis points over U.S. Treasuries on Tuesday compared with quoted levels of 145 basis points before the announcement.
Other markets for the paper were not seen, according to several market sources.

Nevertheless, traders said the market was still undecided where the debt would end up. The completion of the merger and possible downgrades by major ratings agencies still cloud the value of all the company's liabilities, traders said.
"The market will be in the process of assessing what the value of the paper will be until the merger is done," one trader said.

Junk-rated Phar-Mor and ShopKo on Monday said they signed an agreement to combine the two companies under a new holding company in a deal valued at $1.0 billion, including the assumption of debt. The deal will involve share exchanges with the new company, Cabot Noble Inc, with ShopKo and Phar-Mor continuing as separate operating subsidies.
Moody's Investors Service on Monday said it may raise Phar-Mor's B3 senior unsecured debt rating and lower ShopKo's Baa2 senior debt rating.

Standard & Poor's on Tuesday said it may raise Phar-Mor's single-B corporate credit rating and B-minus senior unsecured notes. The agency said ShopKo's BBB corporate credit and senior unsecured debt ratings are under review for downgrade.
